TATA Nexon EV was the most popular choice. The study underlined the importance of developing a more robust EV charging infrastructure. Reuters Representative Image Over 51 per cent electric vehicle owners in India want to return to ICE vehicles , a recent study has found. Park+, a platform hosting approximately 1.5 crore cars and over 25,000 verified e-car owners, has unveiled findings from a recent survey targeting 500 e-car owners in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, and Bengaluru. This study sought to understand the mindset of e-car owners in an evolving electric vehicle (EV) market in India. Key insights from the survey include charging anxiety, maintenance costs, resale value , owner satisfaction, and popular car choices among e-vehicle owners. One of the central concerns highlighted by the survey was charging anxiety, affecting 88% of e-car owners. This issue has surpassed range anxiety , which had traditionally been a significant concern. Despite the presence of more than 20,000 EV charging stations across India, respondents voiced their frustration over the opaque visibility and accessibility of these stations. They emphasized that finding a safe and functional charging station remains a considerable challenge, even as most drivers restrict their intercity journeys to less than 50 kilometers. EV calculator How much will I save if I choose an electric vehicle? SELECT vehicle type Calculate Maintenance costs emerged as another critical issue, troubling 73% of e-car owners. According to the respondents, their electric vehicles often felt like "a black box" that was difficult to understand. Compounding this issue was the inability of local mechanics to solve minor problems. Many e-car owners also expressed frustration over not being able to obtain a clear picture of repair costs due to the lack of multiple repair shop options. A dramatic decline in resale value also surfaced as a significant concern. About 33% of the respondents stated that when they casually checked their e-car's resale value, the quotes they received were much lower than expected. The resale value of e-cars is anticipated to improve as the current EV ecosystem matures. Unlike Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles, which can be easily valued based on age and mileage, there are no widely used tests to determine the quality of an EV's battery, which contributes to 30% of its overall value. Live Events E-car owners generally reported lower levels of satisfaction compared to ICE car owners. The survey revealed that 51% of 4W EV owners would not consider buying another EV, preferring instead to switch back to ICE vehicles, citing everyday hassles involved in owning an EV. Part of this dissatisfaction stems from the industry handling second-hand EVs for the first time. When it came to brand preferences, the TATA Nexon EV emerged as the most popular choice, garnering 61% of the vote, followed by the TATA Punch EV at 19%. Respondents lauded TATA EVs for their design, durability, and safety. BYD also gained considerable attention, although its pricing and the lack of test driving options were noted as significant obstacles for potential buyers. Amit Lakhotia, founder, and CEO of Park+, commented on the survey, emphasizing the company's commitment to enhancing the car ownership experience. "At Park+ our main business objective is to bring delight back to car ownership. This survey is a step in the same direction to understand the mindset of the e-car owners in India. The Indian 4W EV story is still being written and the need of the hour is to build a robust and smart EV charging infrastructure embedded in our current vehicular ecosystem. Charging anxiety has overtaken range anxiety by a huge margin. As the largest EV charger installer in the country we will continue to invest our energies in enhancing the EV car ownership experience for them, throughout the life cycle of their car and look forward to partnering with other external stakeholders to support us in this endeavour." Notably, the study also corroborated the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), India statistics, which indicated that nearly 91,000 electric passenger vehicles were sold during the financial year 2023-24. Other survey insights indicate that the Indian EV market, although developing, still faces challenges that affect owner satisfaction and the overall user experience. However, the potential for improvement appears significant as stakeholders like Park+ aim to tackle these hurdles through better infrastructure and more transparent information dissemination.
